# Setup & Component Choice

## Installation

```bash
npm install @kritzel/react-editor
```

`@kritzel/react-editor` wraps the core `@kritzel/engine` web components in typed React components (generated by the Stencil React output target) and re-exports all classes/types you need â€” import everything from `@kritzel/react-editor`, or from `@kritzel/engine` when intentionally building an engine-only integration.

There is **no app-level setup**: no provider, no plugin, no `defineCustomElements` call. Rendering `<KritzelEditor>` registers the custom elements automatically.

## Global sizing CSS

The editor fills its host; the host must have a concrete size. For a full-page canvas:

```css
/* index.css */
html, body, #root {
  width: 100dvw;
  height: 100dvh;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

```tsx
<KritzelEditor style={{ display: 'block', width: '100%', height: '100%' }} />
```

In a flex-column layout (toolbar above the canvas), size the editor with `style={{ flex: 1, minHeight: 0, display: 'block' }}`.

For mobile, add to `index.html`:

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="viewport-fit=cover, width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1.0, minimum-scale=1.0, interactive-widget=resizes-content" />
```

## Editor vs. Engine â€” decision rule

| | `<KritzelEditor>` | `<KritzelEngine>` |
|---|---|---|
| Toolbar, settings, workspace manager, export UI | âœ… built in (each part hideable) | âŒ none |
| Tools registered by default | âœ… selection, brush, eraser, line, shape, text, image | âŒ **none â€” you must `registerTool` yourself** |
| Readiness event | `onIsReady` â†’ `CustomEvent<EditorIsReadyEvent>` | `onIsEngineReady` â†’ `CustomEvent<KritzelEngineState>` |
| Ref element type | `HTMLKritzelEditorElement` | `HTMLKritzelEngineElement` |
| Programmatic object/viewport API | âœ… full (delegates to engine) | âœ… full |
| Typical use | Default. Hide pieces via `isToolbarVisible`, `isMoreMenuVisible`, `isWorkspaceManagerVisible`, `isUtilityPanelVisible` | Fully custom UI around a bare canvas |

**Prefer hiding editor UI over dropping to the engine.** A "chrome-less" editor still gives you context menus, shortcuts and tool plumbing:

```tsx
<KritzelEditor
  ref={editorRef}
  editorId="embedded"
  isToolbarVisible={false}
  isMoreMenuVisible={false}
  isWorkspaceManagerVisible={false}
  isUtilityPanelVisible={false}
  onIsReady={() => void onReady()}
  style={{ display: 'block', width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
/>
```

## Component skeleton (editor)

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { KritzelEditor, type EditorIsReadyEvent, type HTMLKritzelEditorElement } from '@kritzel/react-editor';

export function Board() {
  const editorRef = useRef<HTMLKritzelEditorElement | null>(null);
  const [isReady, setIsReady] = useState(false);

  async function onReady(_event: CustomEvent<EditorIsReadyEvent>) {
    setIsReady(true);
    // all programmatic API usage starts here, via editorRef.current
  }

  return (
    <KritzelEditor
      ref={editorRef}
      editorId="board"
      onIsReady={event => void onReady(event)}
      style={{ display: 'block', width: '100%', height: '100vh' }}
    />
  );
}
```

`EditorIsReadyEvent` (the `detail`) contains `host`, `activeWorkspace` (`id`, `name`, `isPublic`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), `syncConfig`, `assetStorageConfig`, `loginConfig`, and `theme`.

## Headless engine skeleton

The engine registers **no tools** â€” without registration the canvas accepts no input. Register at least a selection or brush tool in `onIsEngineReady`:

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import {
  KritzelEngine, KritzelBrushTool, KritzelEraserTool, KritzelSelectionTool,
  type HTMLKritzelEngineElement,
} from '@kritzel/react-editor';

export function HeadlessCanvas() {
  const engineRef = useRef<HTMLKritzelEngineElement | null>(null);

  async function onReady() {
    const engine = engineRef.current;
    if (!engine) return;
    await engine.registerTool('selection', KritzelSelectionTool);
    await engine.registerTool('brush', KritzelBrushTool);
    await engine.registerTool('eraser', KritzelEraserTool);
    await engine.changeActiveTool('brush');
  }

  return (
    <KritzelEngine
      ref={engineRef}
      editorId="headless"
      onIsEngineReady={() => void onReady()}
      style={{ display: 'block', width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
    />
  );
}
```

Engine-only extras: it additionally exposes `exportAsJson`, `importFromJson`, `getIsPublic`, `saveSettings`, `loadSettings`, and the `workspace` prop. Editor-only extras: `toolbar`, `customSvgIcons`, `loginConfig`, UI visibility flags, `openLoginDialog`, `setLoginLoading`.

## Prop stability (the React-specific rule)

The wrapper assigns object/array props to the underlying web component **by reference, on every render where identity changed**. Recreating them inline re-runs the component's prop logic and can reset internal state. Therefore:

- Define static config at **module scope**: `toolbar`, theme objects, static context-menu arrays.
- Memoize per-instance config with **`useMemo(() => ..., [])`**: `syncConfig`, context menus that close over the ref.
- Inside memoized callbacks (context-menu actions, control configs), access the editor via `editorRef.current?.` â€” the ref object is identity-stable, so an empty dependency array is safe.

```tsx
const syncConfig = useMemo<KritzelSyncConfig>(() => ({ providers: [IndexedDBSyncProvider] }), []);
```

## Multiple instances

Every concurrently mounted editor/engine needs a unique `editorId` â€” it namespaces settings (localStorage) and persistence (IndexedDB) keys. Without it, instances clobber each other's stored state.

```tsx
<KritzelEditor editorId="left-board" ... />
<KritzelEditor editorId="right-board" ... />
```

## SSR / Next.js

The wrapper components are marked `'use client'` and touch browser APIs (custom elements, localStorage, IndexedDB). In SSR frameworks, render Kritzel only on the client â€” in Next.js App Router import it from a client component; if hydration issues arise, load the canvas component via `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`.

## Common setup mistakes

- Canvas invisible â†’ host element has no size (rule: explicit `display: block` + width/height, or `flex: 1, minHeight: 0`).
- "Method X failed / engineRef undefined" â†’ called before `onIsReady`/`onIsEngineReady` fired, or `editorRef.current` read during the first render.
- Headless engine ignores all pointer input â†’ no tools registered.
- Two boards share drawings/settings â†’ missing distinct `editorId`.
- Editor resets/re-initializes on every keystroke of surrounding UI state â†’ object props (`syncConfig`, `toolbar`, menus) recreated per render; hoist or memoize them.
